node.name: Push Party by Nia Akilah Robinson
node.descriptionText:
About the show: Nia Akilah Robinson’s Push Party is a lively ensemble comedy about six Black women trying to uphold fifteen years of friendship at a post-birthing party in Harlem. All Lelo wants is for this event to go smoothly, but tensions among the group rise and then explode when an unhoused person lands in the community room. Inspired by Black women’s stories of birth and motherhood and by the joys and challenges of life in Harlem, this new play confronts the moments when friendship erodes, when hope starts to falter, when we argue until we laugh, and when Black folk see other Black folk suffering and die a little inside.

Performance Dates and Times:
Thursday, November 5 @ 8pm 
Friday, November 6 @ 8pm 
Friday, November 6 @ 11pm 
Saturday, November 7 @ 4pm
Saturday, November 7 @ 8pm

node.name: Sprout at Yale
node.foodDetails: Pepperoni or Cheese Pizza. Or salad for those with dietary restrictions.
node.descriptionText: Sprout at Yale is a 2-day educational outreach program inviting motivated middle school students from the area to Yale's campus for a weekend of unlimited learning. Sprout's mission is to increase students' excitement for learning by introducing them to topics beyond the scope of traditional school. By harnessing the passion and enthusiasm of Yale students, we hope to inspire high school students to seek out further learning and see education as a fun, inviting process. We want to empower students by giving them full choice regarding their Sprout days.

node.name: Botanical Garden of Healing Clean-Up w/ Urban Resources Initiative
node.descriptionText:
The New Haven Botanical Garden of Healing Dedicated to Victims of Gun Violence was created by the mothers of victims of gun violence as a special place to remember their loved ones. The garden is a place of hope and healing on Valley Street in New Haven, CT. With each new tree and flower planted, the mothers are taking positive action to build public awareness of the magnitude of the problem of gun violence and invest in the future of our community.

Please bring drinking water and wear closed-toe shoes and clothes that you don't mind getting a little dirty!

node.name: Volunteer Clean-Up at New Haven Botanical Garden of Healing
node.descriptionText:
Come volunteer at the New Haven Botanical Garden of Healing Dedicated to Victims of Gun Violence. Our SER student chapter will join URI (Urban Resources Initiative) for their monthly volunteer event to help maintain this beautiful public space. 

The garden is located at 100 Valley Street, New Haven, CT 06515. Parking is available at Elm City Montessori School (495 Blake St). We will be bringing coffee and donuts, and organizing carpool options to leave from Kroon Hall or a meeting spot in East Rock. Please bring drinking water, a sun hat, and work gloves, and wear closed-toe shoes and clothes that can get dirty. Thank you!

Register here on YaleConnect for carpool and coffee, and sign up on URI's page here: https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10c0c49adab2da6f9c16-botanical#/.

node.name: Fall Festivals Around the World
node.descriptionText:
Join us this Saturday, November 7th, for a family-friendly day in the park with arts and crafts! The events will be ongoing. We will be hosting hands-on stations to come learn about and celebrate fall celebrations like the mid-autumn festival, Diwali, and Thanksgiving. This event is open to all ages, and we highly encourage folks to come with their families. Food and snacks will be provided as well!! 

Open to all Yale GPSS students and New Haven community members. 

Meeting at Wooster Memorial Park (the playground between Sally's and Pepe's).
